utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, if you're short in time, is it really that relevant that -- who went there, which president, which prime minister or which minister of foreign affairs. Please move on. What we're interested in primarily is to hear from the witness what he heard or read in statements and how that trigged him to see locations and to make photographs and what he found there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. If you would bear with me, I have a tie-up for this because I share your -- I don't usually like to get involved with ministers in these cases, but there is one tie-up which I think you'll want to see. I may be wrong but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll then hear from -- about that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember the date that you went to the farm with Madeleine Albright?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely not. I reviewed that recently. I think 21st March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Have you had a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did we show you a page of what we told you we believed was a page out of the Mladic diary?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can we see that now. It's P00348. E-court 47, 48, English; 44, 45, B/C/S. English 47; B/C/S 44.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now we can see this diary. And I don't intend to spend much time on this. But it's dated 22nd of March, if your memory is correct, the day after you went there with Madeleine Albright. And we see a note related to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, it just turned into Serbian. If we could see the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps it's not the right page. You said page 47?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This might be the right page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's now the 22nd of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. And we see the note under President Karadzic's name: "A big show was put on for Albright. She expected they would find 1200 Muslim bodies but they found some five bodies."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now when you went there with Madeleine Albright or that time before, did you find any bodies?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. The days we find -- the 19 of March when we went there, we could find -- we could find the site. What we could see moving towards it was shoes, first some shoes. Then some bones, one skull. And when we ended up finding the area of the mass grave, there was one -- obvious body parts on the top of a body that had been pushed by a heavy machine a bit out of the soil, so this body was more or less popping out of the soil. But we did not find five bodies. We find elements of bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did the -- at the time of the investigation, had the -- had the number 1200 come up from any source?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it had come out from press information released, following information provided by Drazen Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And are you aware of -- after your visit to this site with Ms. Albright, did she give any press conferences you're aware of?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she did. She gave a press conference in the evening, in Sarajevo, I think. It was at the US embassy. And the aerial imagery was publicly released that day, the aerial imagery related to the Branjevo farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And just one more reference, I would like to ask you if it had any possible reference to your investigation. As we go down a few more lines we see it says: "Fico was here last night and he says that those two would tell the story about the," crossed out The Hague, "Srebrenica to The Hague." Does -- does that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, may I interrupt you. I read: "... would sell the story ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Ah, I missed that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You said: "Tell the story." In that way it is recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. The next Tribunal I hope will have bigger print. "Sell the story." And that's a very important point, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, does that bit of information have any meaning to you or any possible connection to events at that time and the investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my personal view, this is a direct reference to the fact that since Drazen Erdemovic and Captain Radoslav Kremenovic were under arrest in Serbia and at the edge of being handed over to the ICTY, these are the two ready to sell out the story that the general is referring to in his book. But this is my personal opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on to your discussion further.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is obvious that is not the general who is speaking. I would just for that to be clarified. It is obviously Radovan Karadzic speaking if it is general's book and not the general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let have a look. We see -- we see -- No loud speaking, Mr. Mladic. You know why --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... because of the translations so that's why he's complaining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, who is speaking, at least what we see on top of that, that it says "President Karadzic" and no other interlocutor is specifically mentioned up till where we read this text.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, that's -- the interpretation of all this is a different matter, who is speaking. But unless the witness would know who spoke there, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No. Perhaps -- and I will discuss this with Mr. Lukic, we may be able to agree that this is General Mladic taking notes on what President Karadzic is telling him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm just telling what that note says. It says: "President Karadzic," semi-colon, and it was quoted whoever wrote it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently Mr. Lukic had some concerns as if these words would have been presented as the words of Mr. Mladic; whereas he says that from the document itself, he understands it to be the words spoken by Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. And it's the Prosecution position that we agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So -- apparently there seems to be no conflict there. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we go on. Do we then correct the witness's statement at page 51, line 11, where he says the story that the general is referring to. He is -- he is mentioning the general here whoever the general is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understood to be to the general in writing his notes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I was just -- indeed that was not precise enough --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be full agreement that in this notebook, the author of the notebook refers to the words spoken by Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That being it, please proceed. I'm looking at the clock, Mr. McCloskey. I think it is time for a break. Could we have -- at the same time, perhaps the witness could already be escorted out of the courtroom. Could I have the time from Madam Registrar. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, how much time you think you'd still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would hope, if we get back on track, I -- 30 minutes of testimony. I also have one -- about a seven-minute video of -- of a secondary mass grave exhumation, if I could ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You go beyond your estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sometimes we cannot fit into time constraints, so we do not have objections if Mr. McCloskey needs more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. 40 minutes after the break, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and we'll resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could go back to the -- the book, to e-court page 212.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which the Chamber recognises as exactly the same location as we looked at before on the aerial view. And also, in view of what we have seen on the helicopter view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, we're now back at page 212 and excuse me, if we -- if we -- we are running out of time, so excuse me, if we may go through this. I think we all recognise 212 as the Branjevo farm. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 213. Is this the fruit tree by the garage that you spoke about one of the witnesses told you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. And behind this tree is the open space of the execution site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 214. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the -- the area we now know is the execution site. And this is the first visit we did, the 19. And at the edge of this site, on the left, this is where we found suspect items.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And 19 March --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: March 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Right. Okay. Now, what kind of suspect items?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We will see bones and the skull I was talking about. Shoes. I mean, these elements were found going towards the direction of the location of the grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go there. 215. Is this the shoe you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first thing was just a shoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 216.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then various bones. I'm not an expert but if I recall well it was designated being a piece of a hip, a rib, and a femur.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the skull I was referring to. There is no photograph of body part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And let's go directly to 219, which is similar to 218, but -- but you have made observations on that so let's go to 219. And we see the places you've described, the access, the garage. Now let me start with bodies. Why do you mark what -- you know, is obviously a great distance that -- those little marks as bodies?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only strange thing is the colours, because the markings access to farm and garage are mine. The other ones were white at the origin provided by the provider. The designation bodies, piles of earth, probable bodies, and excavated digging is not something that I added to this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So that's the United States?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the United States.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did the investigation reveal any disagreement with their conclusions?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I couldn't see the probable bodies because they were later on in the grave. The excavator digging, it's -- it's the provider who tells that this is an excavator digging. Same thing for the dots on the ground with dotted line "bodies," and we conducted a search for shell casings on the area marked "bodies" which enabled us to determine the rough size, indeed, of this execution site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 220. What's the purpose -- what does this show us?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This shows that between July 5th and 21st September the soil has changed. The earliest picture being at the right. The arrow shows the change in the terrain, pointing to a now burial area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now we see that the next chapter is called: "The Pilica Dom." Can you tell us how it was that you were attracted to the Pilica Dom for your investigation, briefly?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only source of information for this crime scene was Drazen Erdemovic, since we have no knowledge about any survivor from this Pilica Dom. According to what Erdemovic said, after they had finished the execution at the Branjevo farm, they moved to Pilica village and went to a cafe with a lieutenant-colonel that they had met at the Zvornik Brigade. And meanwhile they were drinking in this cafe, he witnessed the killing of those who were inside this Dom of culture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And after receiving that account, did you go to the -- Pilica and track down the various things he said and -- and is that the next shots in your book?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go there. 223.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So at the left, this is -- the picture is facing north. At the left of the picture is this house of culture, the Dom Kulture. The buses stop in front and the prisoners were taken inside. And the cafe just in front is the one marked with the arrow "cafe."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 224. What's this, this building?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the front facade facing the road of this Dom of culture. On the first floor was also the mayor's office. And at the ground floor, a little communication centre, telephone centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. 225.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an outside view of the cafe that is just opposite side of the road facing the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's -- 226.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a view from the inside of the cafe, so the view that those who were drinking inside had from what was happening outside. One can see that there is a -- a little kiosk obstructing the view that enables to see the entrance door of the Dom of culture, but Erdemovic said that he heard the -- the sounds of the execution and also people who ran out of this and were shot outside on the street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just seek clarification there. You said it deprives the view of the entrance door.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To be quite honest, it looks to me as if it is the car that prevents the view on the entrance door, because the kiosk just covers the area to the corner of the building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whereas the first item we then see is a door which is not totally visible because the car is in front of it. Or is there any other door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There is another door because the entrance is not at the front. It is on the side of the building, just the angle you talked about obstructed by this kiosk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's then move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 227, please. How does this fit into what is being said?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, so the kiosk would be now at our left, just out of the frame of the picture. The front facade that can you recognise but the main important part of it is on the right hand. It is the -- the big room that is used for theatre or cinema.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next page. 228. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the -- the access to the inside of this building. The left door is going upstairs to the first -- to an upper floor, from where the projectionist can show his films. There were two openings at the top of this -- of this building, showing the room inside. We will see that on other pictures. And the door on the -- the metal door on the right is the door -- the entrance door of this Dom of culture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 230.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we had another one before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yeah, I skipped it, but if you think --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it is important.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back. What is -- what's 229?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: 229. So this picture shows the door as we -- the first time we arrived there. There was -- the door was locked and as you can see there are even spider nests in between these doors. The importance of it is that after this place had been cleaned, no one entered it. So we were indeed the first ones to enter this location in 1996. It had not been entered before apparently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that because of the spider nests?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You think that spiders could not create a nest in, well, let's say, three months or six months or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not think that this was indeed done just in two months. I think this was closed at the end -- in 1996 and 1995, and that since then it was not entered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I accept that you believe that. But --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is my assumption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I am exploring its -- you are assuming that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can we go to the next photograph. 230.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So seen from the top floor, as I told you, where the cabin of the projectionist is, this is the site one can have and assume also that this is the location from where the fire was opened on the people inside. According to the lieutenant-colonel Erdemovic was with, 500 people were kept inside this location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next picture. 231.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this one shows the inside of a building, with some holes here, and Mr. John Gerns taking samples.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 232. Is this possible -- possible blood on the wall of the culture centre?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. All this was confirmed as being of human origin. Gives an indication of the type of splashes that were visible on the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And 233. Would that be the same?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And 234?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: 244 [sic] it's the -- at the end of this -- this room where the there is a little staircase going to -- it's again blood-stain and bullet traces. The place was obviously full of these.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. 235.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: And completely at the end, also, these traces which appeared then. And then that is to be explosive residues. Grenades were thrown under the stage where apparently people tried to hide and where we also collected a few items, such as an ID. There is a full film about this first visit, but I bet there is no time anyhow to show it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go to the next, 236. Tell us about this.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this one is a picture of July 17, where we can see at the -- in front of the entrance is a truck that is parked and also tire traces that lead to the back of this building, where there is also a rear door that I didn't take picture of but it's in the film. And this is the cleaning process of this -- and one can assume it is the cleaning process of Dom of culture. But aside this imagery, I learned from the Prosecution that you have a live witness talking about this cleaning process.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, may I ask who made these imprints, track, traces, and rear door.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And on the right-hand lower corner, there's something telling some numbers and then F-e-b, like February. Can you tell us the significance of that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no clue about it. I never asked myself the question what this meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And but for those strange orange markings that somehow became orange in your other pictures, are these consistent that you're marking yellow, the US stays with black and white?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. 237. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this indicates the -- the distance between the Dom and the Branjevo farm, believing that the bodies that were taken from the Dom of culture were brought back to be buried together with the bodies of the Branjevo farm. This is the -- the way the road goes, I mean, the dirt road goes towards the Branjevo farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the survivor, the following day, saw in this area a truck filled with bodies. Probably so going towards this direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you say it's the distance. It ends -- it starts at the culture Dom, it ends with an arrow. So for distance --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's just behind this -- you know, as I said, just behind the hill. In fact, here, you can see the hill line. And just behind this arrow is the slope and the farm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Ruez, your next series of photographs, I think you entitled: "Disturbance photos." Can you briefly explain the -- these disturbance -- why you're -- what part of the investigation is this disturbance? We've seen the -- before the alleged executions, no disturbance, and then afterward we see disturbance. But when you're talking about disturbance now, are you talking about something else; and if so, what?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The disturbances we were talking until now was a comparison between the ground before the events of July. But what happened in 1996 is once the exhumations had started, the -- we quickly realised that where a large number of bodies was expected to be found, only a small number was found. And according to the archaeologists conducting these exhumations, the terrain had been -- these graves were obviously disturbed. So additional imagery requests enabled to determine the event, and then there is another type of comparison to be done between how the ground looked after the initial burial and after possible removal of bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Then let's go there. 240. Now we see Orahovac and we see September 7th. And so we're not talking about July, the execution dates. What does this tell you, this split image, if anything?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. So on the left picture you can see the area which matches the execution site. Top of it is a railroad with exactly the same orientation on 27 September. One can see that the -- the ground has dramatically changed between these two dates. So if disturbance happened, we know from these pictures that the event took place between 7 September 1995 -- I mean, 7 September and 27 September.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell from this photo which of the Orahovac sites we're talking -- we're looking at here?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the site Lazete 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 241. Is this Lazete 1?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Lazete 1, and it's the same situation. The ground doesn't look the same between these two dates. Something happened in between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 242. We're now at the Petkovci dam --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- not very good photos but ...

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But good enough also to realise that again we have -- it's the same angle than the previous one. We have a wood at the left and the top of the dam at the right. And in between these two dates seems to be also some -- some change.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the -- did the archaeologist speak to this issue in the investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did the archaeologist talk about this -- I think as you've said --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. They are the ones who later on will determine the reality and sometimes the extent of the disturbance. At the end of 1996, though several massive graves had been exhumed, only 500 bodies were found at the end of 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go onto 243.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So similar -- similar situation for the Kozluk site. Between 7 and 27, additional disturbance of the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 244.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this picture also dated 27 September. All the markings are provided by the US. There is a blow-up of the area where the garage is located, where it points to a front loader and a backhoe who are present there the 27. And where the grave is located, there is a new excavated trench.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 22 -- excuse me, 245. We see it's a photo labelled "ICTY exhumation 1996." What is this in here for?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this the result of the exhumation done at Branjevo during the summer 1996. The picture shows the entire -- nearly the entire size, the original size of the mass grave, which was nearly empty except at the location where the three persons are standing, where there was a stack of -- a little bit more than 100 bodies that had been left in the grave. But only on -- on this small part of the grave bodies were left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us where this is in relation to the previous picture. We have the newly excavated trench. Is it there or is at any other place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is -- it is there. It is in this newly excavated trench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This shows the stack of bodies that were left in this small part of the Branjevo grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And 247.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The disturbance of these sites did not only happen in the area north but also in the area south. The mass grave of Glogova was also disturbed. And here is a picture dated - we have a series of them but this one was selected - 30 October 1995. There is work ongoing at Glogova which is a large area, in fact, with several mass graves in Glogova. Since the bodies who were taken there were coming from various places, including all those from the Kravica -- I mean, part of those of the Kravica warehouse. And on this picture, the provider spots a front loader who is digging in one of these graves. The other ones on the opposite side are already disturbed when this photograph is taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. You've shown us the -- some of the investigative evidence regarding this -- what you're calling a disturbance of these graves. Were you -- was the investigation ever able to track down where any bodies were taken from this disturbance, from any of these mass graves?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And there will, of course, be others testifying about this but could we briefly go through that. Let's start with 249. We've got the Zeleni Jadar road segment which we may recall is the road leading up to Srebrenica from the south.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What are all these little markings you've done, ZJ-1 through 6, I believe?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. So we had a confidential information about movements of bodies in this area of Zeleni Jadar. Imagery request enabled to add to this information based on which we initially found two suspect spots but in reality there were more in this area to be found. And there are, in fact, six sites connected to this investigation in the area of Zeleni Jadar, which is quite a removed area, a bit dangerous to browse through since there were minefields in this area during the time of confrontation. So it was a remote place. We know that these bodies, in fact, are the result of a disturbance of Glogova site, so they were taken to the opposite side of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question in relation to the previous picture. You told us that this was disturbed earth. And you said since the bodies who were taken there were coming from various places, including all those from the Kravica and part of those of the -- well, so you're telling us that this picture, the previous one, that's the -- let me see, that is ... I think it was [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, 247, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, 247. Let's have a look. Yes, 247. And then you were asked: Do you know where the bodies were taken? I did understand that the bodies were taken here. And Mr. McCloskey then asked you - let me see - he said: "You've shown some of the investigative evidence regarding this -- what you call disturbance. Were you -- was the investigation ever able to track down where any bodies were taken from this disturbance?" Whereas I understood your answer to be that this disturbance, as we see it on our screen now, was the place where the bodies were taken. So were they then taken again from that spot to other places, because that's then a missing -- missing link in the story.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Initially, those who were executed at the Kravica warehouse were buried in a shallow grave nearby but then the bodies were taken to Glogova. Glogova is also the location where the bodies of those killed in Bratunac were taken too. And also an unknown amount of people shot alongside of the asphalt road were collected and Glogova was the final point for these dead bodies in the area. That was the situation by the end of July, but then the disturbance of this place took place, and the content of -- of this grave, of most of it, because in each circumstance bodies were left in these graves, by accident or on purpose, and all the content of Glogova was transferred in six smaller graves at Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I understand. So they were taken sometimes from the place of the execution to Glogova either as the first --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First burial --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- first grave or sometimes even already as a secondary grave because they had been buried already before. And now some of the bodies then were taken from here to their -- either their secondary graves or their second secondary graves.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not really. Because they were not buried yet. Those who were taken here, it was their first burial spot. That spot was first burial spot. Those killed in Bratunac were not initially buried in Bratunac. They were taken to this -- to this location. This was the main location for putting bodies killed in the south --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said initially those who were executed at the Kravica warehouse were buried in a shallow grave nearby but then the bodies were taken to Glogova. So for the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Misunderstanding on my part. I miss explanation. First they were taken to a shallow grave nearby where they left, the exhumation recovered them from that location, but then they changed the destination of the bodies killed in Kravica. And those who had not been put in the first location were all put in Glogova where they were buried for the first time, these ones, and then they were later transferred to Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is clear to me now. Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of that first location as Ravnici?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ravnici, indeed. I didn't remember but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, fundamentally, did the same thing happen at the Orahovac executions, the Kozluk executions, the Branjevo farm executions?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened in all -- all of the places, so yes, the [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I left one out, Petkovci.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Petkovci. It happened on all of these spots. The only spots it did not happen is the Cerska valley, and the two Nova -- the three graves at Nova Kasaba. In two graves Nova Kasaba, one which is in between Nova Kasaba and Konjevic Polje. Because they are small. The assumption is because they are small graves. They disturbed the big graves. A grave with 80 or 100 bodies apparently was not too much of concern. But a grave with hundreds in it was a big concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are invited not to overlap with Mr. McCloskey and to slow down slightly. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that the bodies from Orahovac were -- some were found in secondary graves along the Hodzici road, as you have noted in this book on page 283?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's coming. Sorry. 253. My fault.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, there was a map that could have been useful before, but we can use this. But the map would be of relevance to spot the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 2 -- excuse me, 252.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, yes, indeed. So along this -- this road, we were provided with information from US government linked with imagery with some suspect sites. So each time we received information about suspect sites, the first thing we did was go there and dig in these places. In order to determine if multiple remains were to be found, this is what we did, as like Zeleni Jadar, and so we went to probe these sites. All of these secondary sites were probe found and probed during the year 1997, all of them. So along this road named Hodzici, which was a former road linking with Tuzla. It's a dirt road, remote area, and this is where they were dropped. We now know from the expert reports that these bodies are those coming from Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go to 254. Your map, the Liplje road segment, we see -- we see four. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So again it is the same situation in this area of Liplje, which is also very remote. You have really to find your way in this area. So these -- these sites were probed as well and concluded as being filled with multiple remains, so exhumations could be conducted at a later stage. And these bodies were connected through various elements with the bodies robbed at the grave of the dam.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the -- 255, the aerial image of those -- those four sites. Are those the four sites from your map graphic?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are the sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 256, if we could. We see the same graphic in a place near Cancari. Please explain.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a long valley, approximately -- I mean, some 8 kilometres long, where, in fact, there are 12 graves in this area. On the map, only nine are marked on this part, since these nine are the nine that expertise can connect with the Branjevo farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe my time is up. So I would -- would request be given another 15 minutes so that we can finish. We're very close, as you can see, and I don't intend to ask him about the mosque photos because we have Mr. Riedlmayer, a mosque expert. There's also an example of a secondary grave exhumation which highlights much of what Mr. Ruez has said which I would also like to show you, and I apologise for my poor estimates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Some matters seem to speak for themselves. If we have seen a sequence of maps and then aerial views, then, of course, you would expect that that would depict the same ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may use the time you asked for. And ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 257. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a view of the Cerska valley to give an idea of how the terrain looks like and inhabited area. This is facing direction east towards Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think you said Cerska valley?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said Cerska? I'm sorry, Cancari valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So this is the location of the yellow -- yellow markings from the map graphic?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less. Because, as I said, it's quite a long valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And if we go to 258, we can see what is now -- a similar map graphic as we have seen before, indicating those same locations, I take it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. More or less the same locations. We are going from the right to the left, so from the east to the west. They are -- the first three sites, I didn't talk about them yet. These first three are the ones resulting from the disturbance of Kozluk. As an example of obvious connection, the best is from here, because it's when we started the exhumation of one of these sites that were found among the bodies, stacks of labels and green glass, the labels "Vitinka factory," and this is what then led us to go and visit the site of Kozluk which we had no time to visit before that. So it was only in 1997. So the three first ones later on could be connected through the expertise with the Kozluk sites. All the other ones are coming from Branjevo farm. So there are 12 sites along this road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 259.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the site Cancari 12 which is the -- the one that at the extreme west. It's the first one we probed. We probed and exhumed. You can see the shape of the white disturbance inside this round spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you tell us, is this some kind of blow-up of one of those US imagery products?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is a blow-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. That who did, do you know? Is that something you did or -- I see the yellow on it, C-12.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Let's go to the next page. 260.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just try to understand. This picture is 90 degrees -- it's the left picture, the full left CR-12 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but then it's just turned for 90 degrees. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So let's now go to 260.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So here we have set the base camp for the exhumation and it's the -- it's the shape of the previous disturbance. Now we are on it. You can see our equipment, but mainly here in the middle is the secondary mass grave, Cancari 12. It is clearly visible in the middle of the picture with a little orange backhoe at its right. And the white things on the -- next to the grave are body-bags. The exhumation is ongoing at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 261.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this picture shows how -- how looks such a secondary grave once the surface has been cleaned. It's not necessary, the way of doing for the experts, but on this one, I wanted to make a movie for, in bracket, education for the next teams and it was -- ended up being very useful for court purposes also. So we took the first layer off and this is how looks a full-size secondary mass grave. It's a mixture of bodies who have been moved by heavy equipment already three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, you said -- did you make a short film of this -- a good part of this exhumation by the archaeological team of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, we have cut this down. I -- from, I think, its original 20-some-odd minutes to seven or eight minutes. I would request the Court's permission to play it and Mr. Ruez could provide a narrative about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we try, then, to finish this all at the time of the next break, which would be in ten minutes from now, approximately, and then after that we will start the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It is 65 ter 22442B.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's apparently in two parts, so let's start with A, if we could. 22442A.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the beginning of the operation. The first step was to bring in a mine-clearing team, and once this was checked for mines, exhumation could start. So the first thing is to take away the first layer of soil. And then depending on the colour of the soil determine the limits of the grave. The soil becoming greenish because of the decomposition of the bodies. So here Professor Wright is determining the size of it. Then they start digging at the edges, before the little backhoe begins his own dig.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you ID -- we don't need to stop it, but Richard Wright?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Richard Wright is the one who is conducting this exhumation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is he wearing? I think it is pretty distinctive.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: A hat. So when they dig a trench around the grave in order to be able to -- to move into it ... in the -- in the same process also metal detectors are used in order to find shell casings. Might see that a bit later. So it starts with -- with equipment, but then soon as they arrive at the layers of bodies, the work is getting fine-tuned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who are the team members? Are they labourers? Are they -- what are they?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they are not labourers. They are -- I mean, Richard Wright will provide much more explanation than me. No, no, they are archeologists. Here they work on a grave, but, in other circumstances, they work on very, very old bones. Some elements are protected during the dig. This is a hand. Every item is labelled, photographed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now we go to the same number but B.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a -- show how they document the elements inside, which explains also why it is a slow process. Can you hear the sound of a metal detector here now, finding shell casings. The shell casings will later be compared with those found from the primary graves. It is one of the elements that enable to do connections, among other things. This is a foot. The reason why we focus on it is that we found this foot when we did the first probe of the grave and here it is again. When we probe, we just re-close the hole. We never take anything out of it. So the work for them is very hard because it's a junk [sic] of half-decomposed bodies so very hard to extract. Sometimes they spend a lot of time removing a body part from another one. It's -- the film in its length shows it but it is quite exhausting activity. This is the full -- full size of the grave seen from the top. Quality of the image is now a bit -- a bit weird. But you can see all the elements, skulls, clothing. Blindfolds and ligatures were also part of the key elements to connect sites with -- each with another. So here is an example of the difficulty that they have to separate the parts. Knowing that in some instances the bodies are not complete because they have been moved with heavy equipment three times: For the burial, for the unburial, for the reburial. And all of them, as you know are DNA tested.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to finish up the book you've taken some photographs of -- of the mosques in various stages of destruction that you have added to the end of the book as well.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, that finishes my direct. I do have to offer a few things into evidence, the last movie we've seen, the book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the last movie consisting of two parts. But perhaps we start with the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. The -- the book is 65 ter 28756.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? No objections. Madam Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28756 receives number P1132, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1132 is admitted. The last picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the -- the movie, 22442A and 22442B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Receive what numbers, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Numbers P1133 for A, and P1134 for B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1133 and P1134 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we -- could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness wait for one more second. Judge Moloto has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: At page 229 of the book, we have three pictures there. One is called Cerik road segment and another one is Hodzici. Could you give us the name of the first one? It's not -- it's cut off when it got photocopied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's 229 in the hard copy, I take it, which would be in --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 229, yeah, I have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that would be, in e-court -- yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 253. Thank you, Mr. Lukic. No, 253 seems to be a wall with blood on it. In e-court that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It should be 253 by my records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 253. Let's have a look. Yeah, it's on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes ... the name of the first one you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The one that is cut at the top, the Hodzici road segment. Then the one in the middle, Hodzici road segment. They named the third one Cerik road segment but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The first one. Not the -- those two we can read. I'm asking you about the first one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hodzici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it the same as the second?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But the third is the same also. It's a continuation. We just call this entire stretch Hodzici, and for the other parts coming from another location, Liplje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We never use Cerik. It's Hodzici for the entire area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, when you said 253, you were right. I looked at 235, so it was my mistake. Apologies for that. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, after the break you will start your cross-examination, although it will be only very limited today, I take it. Could I remind you that, as the Chamber, I think, has abundantly shown also during the examination-in-chief, that this witness is not a witness of fact on what happened. But whenever he says, This happened there and that happened there, it became clear to us now that what he intended to say is that: This is what I heard from witnesses which triggered me to go there or to take a photograph, et cetera. So, therefore, I think the cross-examination should -- when cross-examining the witness, you keep this clearly in mind that that is the gist of the evidence of this witness. We'll take a break and we'll resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Usually I use the time for reading some decisions, but I have none at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know that you have been expecting for your testimony to be finished this week, but, unfortunately, we shall have to bother you to come again.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have P1132 in e-court. That's the book compiled by Mr. Ruez. And let's go immediately to page 44.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: E-court, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you know, this is an image received from the US Administration. It is said that these are people in a football field. And the other day, we had a witness, RM346, testifying here the other day and he confirmed that this was approximately the size of the group in which he himself was. Now what I'm interested in is, whether you have checked, by any method whatsoever, how many people were put together in these two rectangulars, one is a longer rectangular and the other is a wider one and the people who were put there were prisoners?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We -- I never made an attempt to make a count of these people. There are not enough references to do it. I don't -- I could not say, you know, what would be the size of a pixel that would represent one man, what would be the total number of these pixels. Is it the same if a man is standing? Is it the same if he is sitting? I don't know. So making -- for me, an attempt to count them would be not necessarily irrelevant but too unprecise to be discussed. I would not try to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The witness said that the people in the bigger rectangular were the ones who were sitting on the ground, whereas the people who were in this smaller one were standing up. But, at any rate, all I wanted was to confirm whether you dealt with the numbers of the persons there or not.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And an additional reason is also that I personally have no certainty through a witness statement that this was only a one-event situation. It might very well be, since witnesses who were driving along this road at various times talk about prisoners on this field. I don't know if this field was emptied one hour later and re-filled after with new prisoners. I have no idea. So we can just consider this a situation at a very -- I mean, not very precise because it is approximate 1400, I mean, 2.00 p.m. I don't know what would be the situation two hours later, what it was two hours before. I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We see in this picture that there is no fence at all around this football field; is that correct? And did you receive this information from the witness to the effect that no fence existed there?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could easily check with ground picture I took in April 1996. But I believe you are right, there is no fence in this location.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree that the people were taken prisoner, whether in combat or have surrendered, and were gathered in the locations that were closest to the path along which the column was travelling?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is what occurred, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have photo 58 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Again, we can see another aerial photo, and it has also been claimed that there's a group of people depicted in this photo. And I have the same question about this photo as I did for the previous one. Did you establish how many people were in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer will be slightly different since we have one more specificity on this picture which is the angle under which it was taken. And I explained during the direct, showing the photographs connected with this site, the people here are on a slope. At the moment, the slope is quite steep. So due to this angle, in fact, the -- the group is larger than visible on this picture. If we had the picture from the opposite side, the length would be bigger. Here, you have a part where, because of the line of sight, it seems to be less people than it actually is. But, again, trying to count is a, to me, with this quality of picture anyhow, mission impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I might not have been quite clear in my questions relating to both pictures. What I had in mind was that that could have been determined according to the size of the space that you yourself saw on the ground, as well as on the basis of the fact that the photos ... or rather, in the footage provided by Zoran Petrovic one can see people sitting on the ground. But, in any case, you never tried to establish the exact number of people who were at this location; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not correct. It's not that I never tried to established. It is not possible to establish with the pictures that we have. In my view, it is not possible, but if someone is willing to do it, I'm fine with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is another unfenced area; correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are talking about prisoners. From the witness testimonies that we had an opportunity to review and from the documents from the Muslim side, I'm going to tell you now how many prisoners there were in total, and that is the figure that we arrived at. And if you disagree, please tell me so, and tell me or can you quote a source that speaks differently. In Potocari, 800 men were singled out, or separated. In the Sandici meadow, not more than 1500 people. Konjevic Polje, 100 people. Nova Kasaba, 1500 people. And individual captures totalling 100 people. And another 50 in Luke. Which makes a total of 4.050 people. Do you have any knowledge that, at that time, more people were taken prisoner and in which locations were these people held?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you are asking a question of this witness -- but perhaps he -- he certainly will answer that question. This witness says, This is what I saw, this is what people told me, true or not, but that made me go to this place. I saw a meadow. I think if you would insist that he would say that what we see on our screen now is not 20.000 people because 20.000 people would not fit in whatever way on such a meadow. But we are starting from facts. You are saying, Well, on the basis of this and this and this, and then you mention a lot of places and say, We think that so many were there, how could we fit the two together? If you have a solution for that, I'm quite happy. Ask your question. But this witness says, first of all, that he cannot, on the basis of his material he cannot conclude anything. So, therefore, how possibly could he comment on the unsourced figures you are giving?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was talking about the witness statements in which this witness took part as well. If he cannot answer my question, I will move on. But if he can give us some estimate, I would happily hear from him. But if Your Honours think that I shouldn't ask this question, I will move on, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if the witness -- let me say the following: If the witness can answer the question, I'd like to hear his explanation why he think he can but -- therefore I leave it to the witness. Mr. Ruez, can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Answer is no, but I must admit that I'm already extremely satisfied that coming from the mouth of the Defence there is an admittance of having already captured 4.000 prisoners --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- I think this is the first time we hear this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that is a matter which is not for a witness. Perhaps you are thinking about your past times when you worked for the Prosecution, but whether you're happy or not with any admission by the Defence is not a matter I expect -- although it is perhaps triggered by the question, but it is not a question which is for a witness to further assess. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't our assessment. It is the testimonies of other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, now you make it quite complex. But let me see how you introduced this question, Mr. Lukic. I'll have a look at the transcript exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was talking about the witness statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "I'm going to tell you now how many prisoners there were in total." Not how many they said there were in total but -- "and that's the figure that we arrived at." So let's move on and let's just assume that you intended to say that these are the numbers you reached --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Given by the witnesses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you reached when --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Analysing witness statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Can we now please have page 63 in e-court. It's the valley of Cerska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, is it true that there is a series of witnesses who are giving all various accounts of this one and the same incident? Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is one witness who is, let's say, the main witness who saw the three buses followed by the APC and then by the excavator entering the valley and who, sometime later, heard intense shooting coming from that direction. Now, he's the witness. The other ones are not direct witnesses of this event. They could assist us by trying to pinpoint the location in this valley, but they didn't see or hear anything from this event. There is only one person who actually saw this convoy entering the valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 1D854, briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What we will see is a transcript from the trial of Popovic et al, and it's your testimony of 8 September 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 65 in e-court. It's 1392, the page of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In lines 6 and 7, answering about this specific location, you said, [In English] I quote: "There is, in fact, a series of witnesses who all have a different approach of the situation." [Interpretation] Your evidence in this case prompted me to put that previous question to you. In other words, is there indeed a series of witnesses who have different accounts of the situation or not?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat, one is, let's call him, the key witness who saw the buses, the APC and the excavator entering the valley, but when I say "a series of witnesses," it's a series of witnesses that enabled us to locate the position of the execution and the burial. One who then entered the valley and walked in a pool of blood, and mainly two others who stood hidden at the end of a valley, well, one probably one week later, made a u-turn and smelled the stench of the bodies. And when we showed them a video of this valley, driving from -- all along each side could at one point, the reference point, I think, was a fountain, indicate us the area. And then by going into we could locate the thing by searching all the side of the thing. To tell you detail, what was suspect on this site was that there were branches put on it but they had nothing do there. And the fact is that later on, mainly with the secondary sites, branches being put on top of the soil was one indication that we were not far away from the targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have Mr. Ruez's book back, P1132. We need page 72 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said about this photograph that it was identified by Jose Baraybar, that is to say, that he identified human remains based on photographs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not right. This exhumation and in this probe -- this is a probe, it's not an exhumation. It's a probe to check if indeed we are on a grave, and if it is a grave, that there are multiple remains. After this dig, we refilled the holes, and later on the full exhumation was done, and it was done by -- I think it was Mr. -- it was Bill Haglund who -- I don't remember who did it. I mean, it was done by either Mr. Bill Haglund or by Professor Richard Wright, not by Jose Pablo Baraybar. I mentioned Jose Pablo Baraybar about pieces of bones found at the plateau of the dam. I don't think I mentioned Baraybar for this. He was not with us on this probe.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D855, please. Can we call it up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's your testimony of 11 September 2006 in the Popovic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 4, which corresponds to the transcript page 1421.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Lines 1 through 4: [In English] "We were not with the pathologist that day but it was our assessment, and the picture was later shown to Jose Pablo Baraybar, an anthropologist who was with the team and who identified the human remains according to the pictures." [Interpretation] Does this refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. Jose Pablo was not -- I mean, he was an anthropologist who was with the team but not that day. The pictures were showed to him later. Because even though you have a human skull with clothing in it, and that anyone would be able to say, that, yes, it is a human being in this clothing, we do not have -- I mean, I do not have the expertise to say that the -- it's a human being. So we have to show the -- the photograph to a specialist who can say, yes, it's a human skull. And a skeleton or whatsoever. But, again, this site is fully exhumed. There is a full report stuffed with details about the bodies, the possible cause of death, the way they were found bounded, some even had their feet bounded, and so on, so ... And, yes, it is confirmed that the remains that were found during this probe were human.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question had to do with the methodology applied by Jose Pablo Baraybar. That's all. Because he will be coming here and I just wanted to establish whether it was on the basis of these photographs that he came to the conclusion that these were human remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now ask that we look at page 76 in e-court. Though not in this document. Rather, in P1132.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the introduction to Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need the next page. Page 77. A moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These are the locations that are not related to the sports field in Nova Kasaba; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they are not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that same time, or perhaps not at that same time, people were gathered at the field in Nova Kasaba; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That same day, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: However, at both these locations, on this image, these people cannot be seen.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They cannot be seen because, at this moment, there is no disturbance, but this is a location where an execution will take place. Three groups of 30 people have been mowed down by automatic rifles in the square box that you can see on this picture and the two locations are connected with this massacre. There is a witness of this who saw the scene with his own eyes. And the pathologist who will describe the content of these graves will even be able to implement the fact that some of these people were shot inside the grave. But I didn't enter this detail during the direct. We skipped this episode. Three times 30 people was probably not big enough. And this was 13 July. More or less at the same time of the soccer field. All these things happened more or less at the same moments.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I'm interested in. How did you establish that it was happening at the same time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you're exactly doing what the Chamber tried to avoid you to do. We always said what triggered this witness, what did he hear, what did he find which triggered him to go there or ask for specific aerial views, and now you are asking him to evaluate the testimony of those witnesses. That's where I interrupted several times in the examination-in-chief, and I --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. My mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I think we cannot proceed anymore if you want to escort the witness before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then, I do understand that you ... Mr. Ruez, I make a similar comment to you. In your last answer, you started evaluating why and even commenting on matters --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm not commenting on matters. I just say that we have a crime scene here involving 90 people. We have all the forensic evidence. If the Defence wants to ask questions about details I was not providing during cross, I am very happy to develop much more about these crime scenes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I heard you also say 30 is not enough. That is comment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We make a selection for this trial --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- that we have to summarise things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a comment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. That's a comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's try to -- I think you have heard me say several times, both during the examination-in-chief and now once or twice in cross-examination, what the Chamber considers is the gist of your evidence and let's try to stick to that. We do not know when you'll be re-called for further cross-examination, Mr. Ruez. But, at the same time, even if -- is this an unknown period of time, I have to instruct you that during that period of time, you are not allowed to speak or communicate in any other way with whomever, including former colleagues which might be very attractive to do so, but you are not allowed to discuss or communicate about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given. If there's any exception to be made, then it should be clearly explained to the Chamber why it is and what it is, because I can imagine that your presence in The Hague may be very practical for other purposes. The Chamber needs to be informed about it and the Chamber has to give its consent, and the Chamber will also invite the Defence, then, to comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Could we have permission for him to -- for our witness person Maria Karall to speak with him about logistics as opposed to going through the Victims and Witness, because it is easier for her to just speak to him directly about days and availability and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, purely about logistics, when, how, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is then allowed. So we'll see you back, don't know where -- we do know where but not when.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Regarding the when because of the strict rules that I know and that I am bounded with and I apply them, the shortest would be the better, indeed, because staying under oath for too long period of time is a bit problematic indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You are to some extent in the hands of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn for the day and will resume on Tuesday, the 16th of April, in this same courtroom, I, at 9.30 in the morning. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 16th day of April, 2013, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.17 p.m.,
